title: Week 9 · Overview — The gravity well · Marble roller coasters
bodyHtml:
Academic week of Monday, January 4, 2027 · 5 days · ≈9 B/C meetings · Phase 2: Move it — Energy · energy-transfer · Core week

El pozo de gravedad · Montañas rusas de canica

The week in one paragraph

An orbit is an energy graph: height is potential, the rest is kinetic or lost. The shop builds the graph out of card stock and runs a marble through it. Before the loop goes in: how high does the start have to be for the marble to make it round? Locked, then built.

Learning targets

I can…Puedo…TypeWhat counts as evidence
I can trace energy from height to speed along a track and say where it is at any point.Puedo seguir la energía desde la altura hasta la rapidez a lo largo de una pista y decir dónde está en cualquier punto.Knowledgerecall or recognition — a selected response or a labelled diagram is enough
I can predict the minimum drop height for a loop of a given size before I build it.Puedo predecir la altura mínima de caída para un rizo de un tamaño dado antes de construirlo.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it
I can report the energy lost to friction as a fraction of the starting energy.Puedo informar la energía perdida por fricción como una fracción de la energía inicial.Skillwatched while it is done, or read off the numbers it produced
I can read a track as an energy graph: height is potential, the rest is kinetic or lost.Puedo leer una pista como una gráfica de energía: la altura es potencial, el resto es cinética o perdida.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it

Scored 1–2–3 per target (Marzano) on the reasoning artifact, lowest-dimension rule across the four dimensions. Targets carry Spanish in the app (statement_es), so the paper rating strip and the screen match.

Language objective (posted, tracked, never graded)

WIDA domainLevel 1 (Entering) will…Level 3+ will…Student line (ES)
ReadingRead heights off the track diagram and match high = potential.Read the energy graph and explain the loop minimum.Leo alturas en el diagrama.

Read aloud at the start of every block with the content objective. Recorded met / not yet on the walk-around, by name, and reported to the ELL team — never in the physics grade.

The asteroid thread

What the shop knowsHow this week connects
Phase 2 opens. The analysts describe 2026-XJ's path as falling into and climbing out of the Sun's gravity well — an energy account, not just a track.A track is a gravity well you can hold. The minimum drop for a loop is the same accounting as the minimum speed to escape or to stay in orbit.

The arc of the week

DayHands (first)Into the app
1
Mon 4 Jan		Build the straight run; measure marble speed at the bottom with a photogate; compare to the heightHeight vs. speed table
2
Tue 5 Jan		Predict the minimum drop for the loop; lock itLocked prediction with an energy reason
3
Wed 6 Jan		Build the loop; find the real minimum by lowering the startPredicted / actual
4
Thu 7 Jan		Loss as a fraction of starting energy; where does it go?Loss fraction and where
5
Fri 8 Jan		Reasoning artifact + rate yourselfThe artifact

Every meeting: hands → record → talk (pairs, either language) → write (the tiered frame). Each segment ends with something saved. For this section the app is the packet — there is no paper page to copy.

Reasoning artifact — the graded evidence

Your predicted minimum drop for the loop, the measured one, and the difference expressed as the fraction of starting energy that friction took.

Tu altura mínima de caída predicha para el rizo, la medida, y la diferencia expresada como la fracción de la energía inicial que se llevó la fricción.

Off-week question

Where in your trade does something go up so that it can come down with energy? (A pile driver, a hammer, a load on a hoist.)

¿Dónde en tu oficio algo sube para que pueda bajar con energía? (Un martinete, un martillo, una carga en un montacargas.)

Issued on the last day, nothing due, nothing late. It opens the next on-week.

Materials and tools

Roller-coaster card-stock templates, marbles, Vernier photogate

Order, borrow or build anything missing during the off-week before this one — the shop week is the only slack in the calendar. Put the week's six to eight words on the bilingual word wall with icons before day 1.

Vocabulary — the wall, the lesson, the glossary and the games all read this list

TierWordEspañolWhat it meansIn this week
1drop (noun)caídaThe height the marble falls from.Find the minimum drop for the loop.
1loop (noun)rizo / bucleA full circle of track.Will the marble make it round the loop?
2minimum (noun)mínimo ≈The smallest amount that still works.The minimum drop is where the marble just makes it.
2fraction (noun)fracción ≈A part of the whole, like 1/4 or 25%.Friction took what fraction of the energy?
3energy (noun)energía ≈The ability to make something move or change.Energy moves from height to speed.
3potential energy (noun)energía potencial ≈Stored energy from height.At the top the marble has potential energy.
3kinetic energy (noun)energía cinética ≈Energy of motion.At the bottom it is kinetic energy.
3conservation (noun)conservación ≈The total stays the same; energy only changes form.Conservation: what is lost from height shows up as speed or heat.

Beck tiers: 3 is the physics word, 2 is the academic verb the frames are built from, 1 is the everyday word the demonstration needs. ≈ marks a cognate — say it as one out loud. ≠ marks a false friend — name the trap before it bites. Never introduce a word without the object in hand.

Standards

HS-PS3-1, HS-PS3-3

Where this week lands — Phase 2 mastery task

This week's artifact is evidence toward pp.t2.mastery-where-the-energy-went, the Phase 2 mastery task. The full task is on the overview for the last week of this phase.

The rules that do not change

  1. Hands first, always. The block opens with the object doing the thing. The explanation arrives after there is a result to explain — never a mini-lecture the build is waiting behind.
  2. The prediction is locked before the test, and it is scored on the reasoning, never on being right.
  3. The reasoning artifact is the grade. Whether the bridge held is recorded on its own product target and is never folded into the reasoning score.
  4. Spanish evidence is full evidence. A labelled diagram, a frame from the word bank and a spoken explanation in Spanish earn a 3 on a physics target exactly as an English paragraph would. Say it out loud, in both languages, every week.
  5. Nothing is graded that a WIDA Level 1 student could not have reached. Walk the artifact as that student before you rate anyone.

Full spec: the SEI access layer and the year map in the Claude project. The four-segment block — hands · record · talk · write, about 25 minutes each — is the shape of every meeting.

No day-by-day plans written for this week yet. Say the word and they get the same treatment as Weeks 1 and 2: segment timings and materials, the Spanish for the day, the formative checks and the misconception to press.

title: Week 10 · Overview — The shelter wall · Balsa stick framing
bodyHtml:
Academic week of Monday, January 18, 2027 · 3 days · ≈5 B/C meetings · Phase 2: Move it — Energy · structures · Support week (no new core target)

La pared del refugio · Bastidor de balsa

The week in one paragraph

If a fragment of 2026-XJ comes down, what does a wall have to do? Three days, a templated build, and the direct link to the trades section: frame it — plates, studs sixteen on center, a header — then push it sideways before and after sheathing.

Learning targets

I can…Puedo…TypeWhat counts as evidence
I can trace the load path from the top plate through the studs to the floor.Puedo seguir la ruta de la carga desde la solera superior por los montantes hasta el piso.Knowledgerecall or recognition — a selected response or a labelled diagram is enough
I can predict what a bare frame does when pushed sideways, and explain why sheathing stops it.Puedo predecir lo que hace un bastidor sin forro cuando se empuja de lado, y explicar por qué el forro lo detiene.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it
I can explain why studs are sixteen on center and measured to centers.Puedo explicar por qué los montantes van a dieciséis pulgadas entre centros y se miden a los centros.Knowledgerecall or recognition — a selected response or a labelled diagram is enough
I can build a wall section from a framing plan without asking what a symbol means.Puedo construir una sección de pared a partir de un plano de bastidor sin preguntar qué significa un símbolo.Skillwatched while it is done, or read off the numbers it produced

Scored 1–2–3 per target (Marzano) on the reasoning artifact, lowest-dimension rule across the four dimensions. Targets carry Spanish in the app (statement_es), so the paper rating strip and the screen match.

Language objective (posted, tracked, never graded)

WIDA domainLevel 1 (Entering) will…Level 3+ will…Student line (ES)
ListeningFollow one-step framing directions with a gesture.Follow the framing plan without a demonstration.Sigo instrucciones de un paso.

Read aloud at the start of every block with the content objective. Recorded met / not yet on the walk-around, by name, and reported to the ELL team — never in the physics grade.

The asteroid thread

What the shop knowsHow this week connects
Phase 1 gave the shop trusses. A wall is a truss with the triangle hidden inside a rectangle.A shelter wall's job is a load path and shear resistance. Racking the bare frame, then the sheathed one, shows where the triangle was hiding.

The arc of the week

DayHands (first)Into the app
1
Mon 18 Jan		Frame from the plan: plates, studs at 16 o.c., a headerLoad-path sketch
2
Tue 19 Jan		Rack the bare frame (predict first); sheathe one side; rack againPredicted / actual racking
3
Wed 20 Jan		Why triangulation was hiding in a rectangle; reasoning artifact + rate yourselfThe artifact

Every meeting: hands → record → talk (pairs, either language) → write (the tiered frame). Each segment ends with something saved. For this section the app is the packet — there is no paper page to copy.

Reasoning artifact — the graded evidence

Your prediction of what the bare frame does when racked, what it did, and why the sheathing changed it — with the hidden triangle drawn.

Tu predicción de lo que hace el bastidor sin forro al empujarlo de lado, lo que hizo, y por qué el forro lo cambió — con el triángulo escondido dibujado.

Off-week question

Look at a wall being framed or a stud wall opened up. Where is the shear resistance actually coming from?

Mira una pared que se esté armando o una pared de montantes abierta. ¿De dónde viene realmente la resistencia al corte?

Issued on the last day, nothing due, nothing late. It opens the next on-week.

Materials and tools

Balsa, glue, framing plan, card stock for sheathing

Order, borrow or build anything missing during the off-week before this one — the shop week is the only slack in the calendar. Put the week's six to eight words on the bilingual word wall with icons before day 1.

Vocabulary — the wall, the lesson, the glossary and the games all read this list

TierWordEspañolWhat it meansIn this week
1wall (noun)paredA vertical structure of a building.Frame the wall from the plan.
1sideways (adverb)de ladoTo the side, not up or down.Push the frame sideways.
2plan (noun)planoA drawing that says how to build.Build from the framing plan.
2follow (verb)seguirDo what the plan or the direction says.Follow one step at a time.
3stud (noun)montanteA vertical framing member.Studs are sixteen inches on center.
3load path (noun)ruta de la cargaThe route a load takes from the top to the ground.Trace the load path from the plate to the floor.
3shear (noun)cortante / cizallaSideways force that makes a rectangle lean.Sheathing resists shear.
3racking (noun)deformación lateralA frame leaning into a parallelogram under shear.The bare frame racks; the sheathed one does not.

  4. Spanish evidence is full evidence. A labelled diagram, a frame from the word bank and a spoken explanation in Spanish earn a 3 on a physics target exactly as an English paragraph would. Say it out loud, in both languages, every week.

title: Week 11 · Overview — Propulsion efficiency · Lou-Vee air cars
bodyHtml:
Academic week of Monday, February 1, 2027 · 5 days · ≈9 B/C meetings · Phase 2: Move it — Energy · energy-transfer · Core week

Eficiencia de propulsión · Carros de aire Lou-Vee

The week in one paragraph

The impactor's engine stores energy and delivers some of it. How much, and where did the rest go? The shop's engine is a rubber band and a propeller. Measure what the band stores, measure what the car gets, report the efficiency, then attack the biggest loss.

Learning targets

I can…Puedo…TypeWhat counts as evidence
I can find the energy stored in a rubber band from its force–stretch curve.Puedo hallar la energía almacenada en una banda elástica a partir de su curva fuerza–estiramiento.Skillwatched while it is done, or read off the numbers it produced
I can find the car's kinetic energy at best speed and the power the band delivered.Puedo hallar la energía cinética del carro a su mejor rapidez y la potencia que entregó la banda.Skillwatched while it is done, or read off the numbers it produced
I can report efficiency as energy out over energy in, and say where the rest went.Puedo informar la eficiencia como energía de salida sobre energía de entrada, y decir a dónde fue el resto.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it
I can choose which loss to attack in the redesign and defend the choice with my numbers.Puedo elegir qué pérdida atacar en el rediseño y defender la elección con mis números.Reasoningthe graded evidence of this course — a claim with the evidence behind it

Scored 1–2–3 per target (Marzano) on the reasoning artifact, lowest-dimension rule across the four dimensions. Targets carry Spanish in the app (statement_es), so the paper rating strip and the screen match.

Language objective (posted, tracked, never graded)

WIDA domainLevel 1 (Entering) will…Level 3+ will…Student line (ES)
WritingComplete "Energy in: ____ J. Energy out: ____ J."Write efficiency with where the rest went.Escribo energía de entrada y de salida.

Read aloud at the start of every block with the content objective. Recorded met / not yet on the walk-around, by name, and reported to the ELL team — never in the physics grade.

The asteroid thread

What the shop knowsHow this week connects
The kinetic impactor's budget: energy stored on the pad versus energy that arrives at the asteroid. The analysts want the ratio.Efficiency — energy out over energy in — is the number every propulsion engineer reports. The air car lets the shop measure both sides.

The arc of the week

DayHands (first)Into the app
1
Mon 1 Feb		Build v1; force–stretch curve of the band with the force sensorCurve and area = stored energy
2
Tue 2 Feb		Run: speed with the motion detector or photogate; kinetic energyEnergy in / energy out
3
Wed 3 Feb		Efficiency; list the losses (prop, axle, air); pick ONE to attackLoss list with a choice
4
Thu 4 Feb		Redesign run, locked prediction of the new efficiencyPredicted / actual
5
Fri 5 Feb		Reasoning artifact + rate yourselfThe artifact

Every meeting: hands → record → talk (pairs, either language) → write (the tiered frame). Each segment ends with something saved. For this section the app is the packet — there is no paper page to copy.

Reasoning artifact — the graded evidence

Energy stored in the band (from your curve), kinetic energy at best speed, the efficiency, where the rest went, and the one loss you attacked and what it did.

Energía almacenada en la banda (de tu curva), energía cinética a la mejor rapidez, la eficiencia, a dónde fue el resto, y la pérdida que atacaste y qué efecto tuvo.

Off-week question

Winter vacation follows. Nothing is due. Find one machine at work with an efficiency rating on its plate. What is it?

Siguen las vacaciones de invierno. No hay nada que entregar. Encuentra una máquina en el trabajo con una eficiencia en su placa. ¿Cuál es?

Issued on the last day, nothing due, nothing late. It opens the next on-week.

Materials and tools

Lou-Vee air car kits, Vernier force sensor, motion detector or photogate

Order, borrow or build anything missing during the off-week before this one — the shop week is the only slack in the calendar. Put the week's six to eight words on the bilingual word wall with icons before day 1.

Vocabulary — the wall, the lesson, the glossary and the games all read this list

TierWordEspañolWhat it meansIn this week
1stretch (verb)estirarMake longer by pulling.Stretch the band and read the force.
1spin (verb)girarTurn around fast.The propeller spins when the band lets go.
2store (verb)almacenarKeep for later.The band stores energy.
2efficiency (noun)eficiencia ≈Energy out divided by energy in.Report the efficiency as a percent.
3elastic energy (noun)energía elástica ≈Energy stored in something stretched or twisted.Elastic energy is the area under the force–stretch curve.
3work (noun)trabajo (fuerza × distancia)Force times distance; energy moved into or out of something.The band does work on the propeller.
3power (noun)potencia (≠ poder)How fast energy is delivered: energy per second.Power is the band's energy divided by the run time.
3drag (noun)resistencia del aireAir friction on a moving object.Drag is one of the losses.

Beck tiers: 3 is the physics word, 2 is the academic verb the frames are built from, 1 is the everyday word the demonstration needs. ≈ marks a cognate — say it as one out loud. ≠ marks a false friend — name the trap before it bites. Never introduce a word without the object in hand.

Standards

HS-PS3-1, HS-PS3-3

Where this week lands — Phase 2 mastery task

You are given a machine you have not built — a spring launcher, a pendulum, a dropped mass on a lever — and the probes. Measure energy in, energy out, report the efficiency, and say where the rest went, with one change you would make and a prediction of what it would do.

Te dan una máquina que no has construido — un lanzador de resorte, un péndulo, una masa que cae sobre una palanca — y las sondas. Mide la energía de entrada y de salida, informa la eficiencia y di a dónde fue el resto, con un cambio que harías y una predicción de su efecto.

DimensionWhat a 3 looks like
ScienceEnergy in and out measured correctly with the probes; efficiency computed as a ratio.
ReasoningThe losses named are the ones the data supports; the proposed change attacks the biggest one.
CommunicationNumbers in a table, the story in sentences, in either language.
TransferA machine not built in class, treated with the same energy accounting as the coaster and the air car.

Walk this task as a Level 1 student before it ships: can the prompt be understood from the diagram and the Spanish alone, and can every dimension be met with labels, a frame, numbers and a spoken defence in Spanish? If any answer is no, it is not ready.

The rules that do not change

  1. Hands first, always. The block opens with the object doing the thing. The explanation arrives after there is a result to explain — never a mini-lecture the build is waiting behind.
  2. The prediction is locked before the test, and it is scored on the reasoning, never on being right.
  3. The reasoning artifact is the grade. Whether the bridge held is recorded on its own product target and is never folded into the reasoning score.
  4. Spanish evidence is full evidence. A labelled diagram, a frame from the word bank and a spoken explanation in Spanish earn a 3 on a physics target exactly as an English paragraph would. Say it out loud, in both languages, every week.
  5. Nothing is graded that a WIDA Level 1 student could not have reached. Walk the artifact as that student before you rate anyone.

Full spec: the SEI access layer and the year map in the Claude project. The four-segment block — hands · record · talk · write, about 25 minutes each — is the shape of every meeting.
